headline: LLM pipelines extract structured chemical-effect evidence from biomedical literature
label: Llm Literature Curation Pipelines
summary: Corpus-scale LLM mining now yields continuously updated knowledge bases, with human review retained in hybrid AOP and curation designs.
synthesis: The common thread is LLM-based extraction of structured evidence from biomedical literature. Three preprints address toxicology: AOP-Smart-Finder pairs LLMs and RAG in a human-AI hybrid framework to mine biological events, key event relationships, and AOP evidence; AOPTK is an open-source Python toolkit for LLM-assisted retrieval and extraction of chemical-effect relationships. A further preprint describes an automated, continuous LLM-driven pipeline that mines PubMed/PMC full texts into a 189,212-finding hepatotoxicity knowledge base spanning 17,002 chemicals. What is new is continuous, corpus-scale curation, with human review retained in hybrid designs. KinaseMD 2.0 and the natural-product atlas are adjacent resource efforts; the items do not describe them as LLM-driven.
